questions.q: What is a variable, in Flow terms?
options: A container that holds a piece of information, able to change while the flow runs
A line connecting two elements on the canvas
A fixed value that can never be changed once created
A screen component that displays text
questions.explain: A variable is a container holding information that can change while the flow runs — that's the "variable" part.

questions.q: Where do you go to create a new resource ahead of time, before referencing it in an element?
options: The New Resource button in the Toolbox
questions.explain: New Resource, found in the Toolbox, opens the window for creating a variable, constant, formula, or text template.

questions.q: A tax rate that should never change, and should be defined in exactly one place, is best stored as which resource type?
questions.explain: A constant is a fixed value set once and reused everywhere it's referenced — ideal for a value like a fixed tax rate.

questions.q: What makes a Formula resource different from a Variable?
options: A Formula is calculated from other resources and recalculates automatically when they change
A Formula can only ever hold the number zero
A Formula cannot be referenced by any other element
A Formula is identical to a Variable in every way
questions.explain: A Formula's value is calculated from other resources using functions, and Flow Builder recalculates it automatically.

questions.q: Which resource type is the right choice for building the merged, formatted body of an email or Chatter post?
questions.explain: A Text Template mixes literal words with merged values from other resources, which is exactly what an email or Chatter post body needs.
